newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto Stock Exchange proposes tougher penalties.
newsitem.headline: Toronto Stock Exchange proposes tougher penalties.

text.p: The Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's biggest stock market, said on Wednesday that it plans to impose tougher penalties on brokers and firms that violate trading rules at the exchange.

The TSE said in a statement its board of governors endorsed recommendations by an industry committee to impose stiffer fines and more suspensions to ensure that the exchange's rules are backed by penalties that meet or exceed those imposed by self-regulatory organizations in Canada, the United States and United Kingdom.

The TSE said its board of governors endorsed recommendations by an industry committee to impose stiffer fines and more suspensions in an effort to ensure that the exchange's rules are backed by penalties that meet or exceed those imposed by self-regulatory organizations in Canada, the United States and Britain.

Under the new guidelines, the penalty for trading without a client's prior authorization is disgorgement of any benefit or commission earned by the registered representative, plus a fine ranging from C$1,500 to C$25,000, plus a supervised period of between three and 12 months. A suspension of up to one month could also be imposed under the new penalties. The previous penalty for the offense was a fine of between C$3,000 and C$5,000.

"The establishment of new penalty guidelines illustrates the TSE's commitment to an effective and visible enforcement process which assures investors that they are coming to a well-regulated marketplace," TSE vice-chairwoman of the board Barbara Stymiest said in a statement.
